3.speaker: Iosef Lancea
3.text: “This is a disgrace. Rumburg is at our doorstep and the Armed Forces already have a laundry list of problems. This was a grave mistake that we will surely pay for in time.”

4.speaker: Player
4.text: “Thank you everyone. I appreciate your time and effort.”

5.speaker: Player
5.text: “Regardless of what happened, I wouldn't be here without you. Don't forget that we are a team.”

6.speaker: Player
6.text: “For those who didn't like the decisions, don't take it personally.”

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: Lucian seemed as if he was about to say something, but looked down at his notepad when Iosef eyed him.

11.speaker: Iosef Lancea
11.text: “It is an honor to serve with a President that respects the military. Trust me, with these funds our armed forces will be better than ever before."

12.speaker: Iosef Lancea
12.text: “It is a shame that the military won't be getting an increase. I will have to make sacrifices to maintain our defense.”

13.speaker: Player
13.text: “The continuation of the existing set of budgetary conditions is in order.”

14.speaker: Lileas Graf
14.text: “Thank you for this decision, Mr. President. I knew you would see reason on this, considering our internal security threats are at an all time high.”

18.speaker: Nia Morgna
18.text: “I'm not sure what we'll be able to do if the budget doesn't change.”

19.speaker: Lileas Graf
19.text: “I heavily disapprove. We are barely making ends meet on the security side. I will be forced to reduce our force size and salary.”

20.speaker: Player
20.text: “Our new priorities called for a reduction of law enforcement.”

21.speaker: Nia Morgna
21.text: “The reduction of the budget might also put as in a tight spot regarding our ability to handle the amount of court cases.”

22.speaker: Lileas Graf
22.text: “I suppose we'll have to make do with what we have. This is not the best situation for us.”

23.speaker: Nia Morgna
23.text: “I still disagree with Ms. Graf on how the money ought to be spent, but the increased funding is certainly a step in the right direction.”

25.speaker: Player
25.text: “Maintaining the funding was the correct call especially in light of the threats.”

26.speaker: Player
26.text: “Concessions had to be made with the military budget. The priorities have changed.”

27.speaker: Symon Holl
27.text: “That covers all branches. Each minister will approach you with their respective policy requests and expectations over the next year.”

28.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
28.text: “I'm honestly rather disappointed. The reduction will force us to shut down many hospitals and reduce service quality. It will also reflect badly on us as a government.”

29.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
29.text: “Thank you, sir. This health budget increase will help me to focus on improvements. Our people will now be safer than ever.”

30.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
30.text: “I can't say that maintaining the funding is negative but I don't think our services will perform any better.”

39.speaker: Nia Morgna
39.text: “Exactly. This was a big mistake. I'm so sorry, Ciara.”

40.speaker: Ciara Walda
40.text: “Keeping the same budget will just result in the same problems. However, I prefer this over a decrease. I'll try to reform the system with my own resources.”

41.speaker: Ciara Walda
41.text: “A reduction!? This is the opposite of what we need. Such a shame that this money will go where it's less needed."

42.speaker: Player
42.text: “Education is our future and it will not be sidelined. Our focus on it is clear.”

43.speaker: Ciara Walda
43.text: “Thank you, it is great to see a positive change in the attitude of the administration for the first time in a decade.”

44.speaker: Nia Morgna
44.text: “Surely a well-funded and larger Ministry of Education would benefit everyone.”

45.speaker: Ciara Walda
45.text: “The increase of funding is very welcome. We can finally go after some comprehensive improvements by building new schools and improving the education system.”

46.speaker: Lucian Galade
46.text: “Thank you for your time and participation in this significant moment. The meeting is concluded.”

47.speaker: Narrator
47.text: The ministers bid their farewells -- some excitedly, others dejectedly.

49.speaker: Narrator
49.text: The cabinet slowly dispersed out of the White Room. The budget for our term was concluded.

56.speaker: Iosef Lancea
56.text: “You have kept your promise to focus on the military. An honorable and fitting decision.”

57.speaker: Iosef Lancea
57.text: “On top of it, you did not keep your promise to focus on the military. I will remember this.”

73.speaker: Symon Holl
73.text: “We have a very healthy budget surplus left for investments and other expenditures. Splendid!”

74.speaker: Symon Holl
74.text: “It looks like we have a balanced budget with no deficit or surplus. Not bad. Not bad at all.”

81.speaker: Narrator
81.text: I had finished allocating the government budget, to the satisfaction of some cabinet members and the dismay of others. They and I knew this would define a significant part of our term.

82.speaker: Symon Holl
82.text: “We have a deficit on our hands. We will need to resort to debt to finance future investments. This situation can have adverse effects if we don't strike a balance.”

104.speaker: Narrator
104.text: Ciara clearly wasn't finished, but didn't interject. Iosef chimed in.

105.speaker: Narrator
105.text: Nia and Lileas were both smiling.

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: Lileas leaned forward and put her hand on her chin. Nia was looking down at the floor.

107.speaker: Narrator
107.text: Nia and Lileas were frowning. When I looked at her, Lileas shook her head.

108.speaker: Player
108.text: “The military is on the top of my priority list and always will be. Rest assured.”

119.speaker: Iosef Lancea
119.text: “It will be harder to do so but I shall find ways, it is my duty.”

120.speaker: Iosef Lancea
120.text: “Is there a higher priority than our national security? I doubt it.”

121.speaker: Iosef Lancea
121.text: “The threats called for an increase. Not just a continuation of the same budget.”

122.speaker: Iosef Lancea
122.text: “I knew I could count on your decision-making, Mr. President.”

132.speaker: Player
132.text: “With your talent and experience you will overcome the issues our military faces.”

136.speaker: Iosef Lancea
136.text: “With the support you have provided, I will protect this country from any threat.”

137.speaker: Narrator
137.text: Iosef leaned back in his chair.

138.speaker: Nia Morgna
138.text: “We will tackle corruption and the backlog of cases head-on.”

139.speaker: Lileas Graf
139.text: “We will be able to achieve positive results in the coming year. I can assure you.”

150.speaker: Player
150.text: “Law enforcement is a key branch that needs a greater budget due to the increased threats and need for security.”

154.speaker: Player
154.text: “I trust you to push the Ministry of Interior and Justice forward.”

158.speaker: Nia Morgna
158.text: “Disappointing for the people who want a sense of justice returned. The backlogs won't get solved. The administration will hurt.”

159.speaker: Lileas Graf
159.text: “With the reduction, our work will be hampered and made more difficult.”

160.speaker: Nia Morgna
160.text: “Justice will be served in this nation and having more support is a step in the right direction.”

161.speaker: Lileas Graf
161.text: “We will make a good use of these new resources and fight crime, terrorism and subversives.”

162.speaker: Nia Morgna
162.text: “Troubled times are ahead for our ministries.”

163.speaker: Lileas Graf
163.text: “These are disheartening changes. We will try to mitigate.”

164.speaker: Nia Morgna
164.text: “We may not have the resources to meet new challenges, but I will find ways to help this nation.”

165.speaker: Lileas Graf
165.text: “Our expectations were much higher than this.”

167.speaker: Lucian Galade
167.text: “Well then. Let's start with law enforcement.”

170.speaker: Player
170.text: “Your expertise and passion should enable you to make the necessary changes for improvement.”

171.speaker: Player
171.text: “My expectation is that you maintain education services with the same budget.”

182.speaker: Player
182.text: “This government has defined its priorities, and education is not on the top of the list.”

183.speaker: Ciara Walda
183.text: “Our future depends on our children. Education is the first step in the fight against ignorance.”

184.speaker: Ciara Walda
184.text: “We will be able to achieve my grand goals with these new budgetary resources.”

185.speaker: Ciara Walda
185.text: “It seems we have no other choice but to depend on what little we have. What will our children think of us?”

186.speaker: Ciara Walda
186.text: “It's not even on the list. Cutting our funding will result in disaster."

191.speaker: Ciara Walda
191.text: “Thank you for your confidence in me, but without extra funding we'll have to make sacrifices. And our system will see the consequences.”

193.speaker: Ciara Walda
193.text: “Welfare must remain a priority for our term. There is no other way around it.”

194.speaker: Player
194.text: “Healthcare is very important for us and as we move forward, it will improve drastically.”

195.speaker: Player
195.text: “Your opinions were noted, Paskal. Your task is to improve the care in the country.”

196.speaker: Player
196.text: “It is best we continue our funding as it is. You will have to find new resources.”

197.speaker: Player
197.text: “Sadly, health ended up in the list of budget cuts. Not much can be done about it.”

208.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
208.text: “It feels invigorating to have the weight of the government behind my cause.”

209.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
209.text: “With the new budget we have many options to improve our healthcare program and provide for the people.”

210.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
210.text: “The Ministry of Health will resort to a privatization effort to create funds to improve services.”

211.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
211.text: “It is very unfortunate. I will have to look into privatising parts of our system to create funds in order to maintain operations.”

216.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
216.text: “Which will be very difficult to accomplish without an increase in funds.”

218.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
218.text: “I am also planning to tackle issues like the lack of rural hospitals and the recently worrying numbers of maternal deaths.”

407.speaker: Nia Morgna
407.text: “Here I was thinking the Rayne administration would be on the side of law and justice.”

408.speaker: Lileas Graf
408.text: “Our efforts will be on maintaining order with what we have.”

436.speaker: Symon Holl
436.text: “We have a good budget surplus left for investments and other needs. Very good.”
